verdict.rationale: Missive documents an official MCP server that lets external AI apps like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor act on conversations, contacts, calendar, and drafts with user-chosen permissions. The changelog gives examples of summarizing the inbox, drafting replies, and triaging new conversations, and drafts can also be created through the API. However, the evidence never shows that an external agent can actually send email, so the 'end to end' part is unproven. missing for 10: documented send capability via MCP/API, detail on available MCP tools and triage actions, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an external agent — Claude, ChatGPT, or my own — can read, triage, draft, and send my email end to end through a documented connection

citations.quote: External AI apps like Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor can now connect to Missive through the Model Context Protocol and act on your conversations, contacts, calendar, and drafts, with the permissions you choose.
Ask Claude to summarize your inbox and draft replies without leaving the chat
Let an agent triage new conversations against your CRM before you look at them
Drafts created outside the composer, by the assistant, by a rule, or through the API and MCP server
official MCP server documented at https://missiveapp.com/docs/ai/mcp/server
